title: How to create a new type of board
description:
Start by implementing each of the following functions in order to get the basic functions of a board working:  

* Constructor
* `pin_list()` and/or `pin_search()` depending on how many pins you expect
* `pin_exists()`
* `pin_meta()`
* `pin_fetch()`
* `pin_versions()`
* `pin_store()`

Next get all of the cross-board tests working:

* `test_api_basic()`
* `test_api_versioning()`
* `test_api_meta()`

Check test coverage, and make sure you have extra tests for any specific behaviour that this board should possess.

title: Failure to record all pins version in data.txt
description:
- **Test**: pin into AWS s3, `cars[1:5,]` from default cache and `cars[2+(1:5),]` from another cache path.  Then try to get the versions.
- **Expected**: Two versions corresponding to the two datasets.
- **Observed**: Only the last version can be retrieved using `pin_versions` or `pin_get`

Note: both datasets remain available on S3 and structured properly under `_version/` path, but data.txt only shows the latest. In other word, the issue is with data.txt keeping accurate records.

To repro:

``` r

# Step 1: start with default cache and pin into S3 cars[1:5, ]
#--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
library(pins)

board_register_s3(name = "d1",

title: `rsc_version` will not work under some configurations of RSC
description:
`rsc_version` currently queries RSC server settings for a version string and then attempts to parse with `package_version`. Two problems with this:

- RSC dev builds have `-devNNN-dirty` appended to the end which makes them unparseable
- The [HideVersion](https://docs.rstudio.com/connect/admin/appendix/configuration/#Server.HideVersion) setting is considered a security feature by many administrators and prevents the version from being discoverable.

However, there's not really a better way to do feature detection of pins support for RSC. Therefore, what I'd suggest is turning this into a warning and informing the user that if a deployment failure occurs, that they might want to check their RSC version.

I wouldn't want to make version constraints opt-out, I think too many heavy users of RSC are hiding their version to make this reasonable.

Alternatively, we could trap for a blank version string and fix parsing connect dev build strings, but that doesn't harden us against connect changing its versioning again.

title: Trying to pin on an old version of RSC yields unhelpful errors
description:
Newer versions of RSC (>= 1.8.8) make `CONNECT_SERVER` and `CONNECT_API_KEY` automatically available in the environment. 

When a document that includes `board_rsconnect()` is deployed to an earlier version of RSC, the result is that the `board_rsconnect()` attempts to use `rsconnect` auth and it yields an error that the `rsconnect` package isn't found, probably sending people down a weird rabbithole.

It would be really helpful if `board_rsconnect` could detect if it were on RSC (`R_CONFIG_ACTIVE` env var is set automatically) and then force `envvar` auth, perhaps throwing a helpful error if the env vars aren't detected.

Maybe something like: "RStudio Connect 1.8.8 and newer automatically provide the environment variables `CONNECT_SERVER` and `CONNECT_API_KEY`. Upgrade or provide those variables manually in the environment variables pane."

title: Offline access to pins stored in rsconnect
description:
I've noticed that pins stored to a corporate RStudio Connect server do not interrogate the local cache for subsequent gets when the Connect server is not available.  My expectation was that they would be retrieved from the local cache if the URL was not accessible.

<details>

Is this intended behavior?

Here are the specific errors that I get when the Connect server is no longer accessible:

"Error in curl::curl_fetch_memory(url, handle = handle) : Timeout was reached: [connect.alkahest.io] LibreSSL SSL_read: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, errno 60"

or

"Error in curl::curl_fetch_memory(url, handle = handle) : Could not resolve host: connect.alkahest.io"

A few more details about how this problem arises:

I'm storing and retrieving pins over a VPN connection to a corporate RStudio Connect server. Sometimes that VPN connection is not available for a variety of reasons and I will work locally.

Below is a simple example that flushes out the issue and demonstrates fetching the data manually from cache. It assumes you can make the RStudio Connect server "go away" at one point.

thx!
scott

```{r}
library(pins)
library(tibble)
```

Register the local Connect server (In this example the real server has been replaced with connect.example.com).

connect_version: 1.8.4.2-2

```{r}
pins::board_register("rsconnect", server = "https://connect.example.com")
```

The API key approach is being used so the following *.Renviron* entry is present and was created under the *scicompadmins* Connect account.

    CONNECT_API_KEY=dbiZ9x7qZpqP..blah...blah


Create data for pin

```{r}
my_test_data <- tibble::tribble(
  ~a, ~b, ~c,
  "a1", "b1", "c1",
  "a2", "b2", "c1"
)
my_test_data
```
Now pin

```{r}
pins::pin(
  my_test_data,
  name = "scicompadmins/my_test_pin_data",
  board = "rsconnect"
)
```

Now get the data back (while on VPN)

This will work.

```{r}
roundtrip_on_vpn <- pins::pin_get("scicompadmins/my_test_pin_data", board = "rsconnect")
roundtrip_on_vpn
```

Now disconnect from VPN (or someother way of making connect.example.com not accessible) and try to get the pin.

This will fail.

```{r}
roundtrip_off_vpn <- pins::pin_get("scicompadmins/my_test_pin_data", board = "rsconnect")
roundtrip_off_vpn
```

One of two errors can happen here:

    Error in curl::curl_fetch_memory(url, handle = handle) : Timeout was reached: [connect.example.com] LibreSSL SSL_read: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, errno 60

or

    Error in curl::curl_fetch_memory(url, handle = handle) : Could not resolve host: connect.example.com

I would have expected the PINS package to catch these errors and interrogate the local cached version.

So let's see if we can manually reconstruct from the local cache (VPN still disconnected)

```{r}
connect_board <- pins::board_get("rsconnect")
roundtrip_from_cache <- readRDS(
  file.path(
    connect_board$cache,
    connect_board$board,
    connect_board$account,
    "my_test_pin_data",
    "data.rds"
  )
) %>% tibble::as_tibble()
roundtrip_from_cache
```

This works with the intended result.

</details>

title: Better directory detection semantics and zip behavior (if we keep it)
description:
Current / legacy pins behavior:
- would try to `zip` a directory
- would allow the `zip = TRUE` argument to "force" the zip behavior

However,
- `zip = TRUE` is a confusing way to tell pins "I want to publish a directory, please zip it up for me"
- The implementation using `withr::with_dir()` in the `zip` flow did not work, because it changes the working directory sufficiently to break the inherent directory names / zip name / `.zip` output location, etc.

I had to [change this](https://github.com/sol-eng/immunotherapy/blob/ca020d19cd905676ff5ca4a74fc687f5a0b601c5/2_publish_model.R) (`saved_model` is a directory):
```
library(pins)
library(keras)

# Pin it on RStudio Connect
pins::board_register_rsconnect()
pins::pin(
  "saved_model",
  "peptide_model",
  "Peptide Prediction Model",
  "rsconnect",
  zip = TRUE
)
```

To this:
```
library(pins)
library(keras)
# Pin it on RStudio Connect
pins::board_register_rsconnect()
local_zipfile <- zip::zip("model.zip", "saved_model")
pins::pin(
  local_zipfile,
  "peptide_model",
  "Peptide Prediction Model",
  "rsconnect"
)
```

title: pin_get returns paths to all cached pins including versioned one
description:
Working with a board on connect, I once retrieved an older version using `version = `

```r
> pins::pin_get("cderv/bookdownorg_books_meta", board = "rsconnect", version = 37847)
[1] "C:/Users/chris/AppData/Local/pins/pins/Cache/rsconnect/cderv/bookdownorg_books_meta/_versions/37847/_book_meta.rds"
```

But after, `pins::pin_get()` without `version = ` always returns paths to all cached pinned instead of just the named pin.
```r
> pins::pin_get("cderv/bookdownorg_books_meta", board = "rsconnect")
[1] "C:/Users/chris/AppData/Local/pins/pins/Cache/rsconnect/cderv/bookdownorg_books_meta/_book_meta.rds"                
[2] "C:/Users/chris/AppData/Local/pins/pins/Cache/rsconnect/cderv/bookdownorg_books_meta/_versions/37847/_book_meta.rds"
```

This is with CRAN version above.
Same with dev version and new `pin_read()` (which does provide support for version)

``` r
rsc_key <- Sys.getenv("RSC_BOOKDOWN_ORG_TOKEN", unset = "")
board <- board_rsconnect(server = "https://bookdown.org", key = rsc_key)
pin_read("cderv/bookdownorg_books_meta", board = board)

#> [2] "C:/Users/chris/AppData/Local/pins/pins/Cache/rsconnect/cderv/bookdownorg_books_meta/_versions/36468/_book_meta.rds"
```

I would expect to only have the path of the named pin returned and not also its older versions as I did not specified version argument. More basically I would expect `pin_get` or `pîn_read` to result with only a single path.

I can build a reproducible example with a pin you can access if you need.

title: old bundles are now removed by default in connect board
description:
I encountered a change in behavior recently. It seems that for rsconnect board now `pins::pin()` will automatically remove old bundled versions of pins and only one will be kept. It seems to me a pretty big change because I lost all the old bundled I wanted to keep initially. 

It seems this is because of 
https://github.com/rstudio/pins/blob/421fe6d7e577a0480aca3a6d26ac35672d8e3dd7/R/board_rsconnect.R#L247-L250
which then will trigger the deletion
https://github.com/rstudio/pins/blob/421fe6d7e577a0480aca3a6d26ac35672d8e3dd7/R/board_rsconnect.R#L320-L329

So `board_versions_enabled` seems to have change for default rsconnect board.
I confirm that with this code between two versions (see below reprex)
```r
rsc_key <- Sys.getenv("RSC_BOOKDOWN_ORG_TOKEN", unset = "")
board_register_rsconnect(server = "https://bookdown.org", key = rsc_key)
board <- board_get("rsconnect")
board_versions_enabled(board, TRUE)
```

I did a bisect and I think this comes from the rewrite in https://github.com/rstudio/pins/commit/16ff9ea546ba806c3c8e43f643367206c5ca2a73 where `versions = FALSE` by default which it may not have been the case before. 

Bisect was not exact because of https://github.com/rstudio/pins/commit/436e961c51eb21c8c0b591daae747bfad284afa3 which created error in code. This is with this commits a14c095feef85ee8a5ab03866b21b17e56e856d2, 16ff9ea546ba806c3c8e43f643367206c5ca2a73, 6779a7bf681f2a2e44d6ec1fb285b5b9196b9457, 436e961c51eb21c8c0b591daae747bfad284afa3


<details>
<summary>Reprex to run in the pins project after setting the env var (or change value in function call)</summary>

```r
system("git checkout cc6697279ae8bd19293585a8850bc0f5afff6baa")
#> [1] 0
devtools::load_all(".")
#> i Loading pins
rsc_key <- Sys.getenv("RSC_BOOKDOWN_ORG_TOKEN", unset = "")
board_register_rsconnect(server = "https://bookdown.org", key = rsc_key)
board <- board_get("rsconnect")
board_versions_enabled(board, TRUE)
#> [1] TRUE
system("git checkout 436e961c51eb21c8c0b591daae747bfad284afa3 ")
#> [1] 0
devtools::load_all(".")
#> i Loading pins
rsc_key <- Sys.getenv("RSC_BOOKDOWN_ORG_TOKEN", unset = "")
board_register_rsconnect(server = "https://bookdown.org", key = rsc_key)
board <- board_get("rsconnect")
board_versions_enabled(board, TRUE)
#> [1] FALSE
# restore branch to master
gert::git_branch_checkout("master")
```

</details>

This seems a pretty big change and this could cause issue for a lot of RStudio Connect users that where relying on bundles being saved. Currently, the workaround is to explicitly change the board registration to set version to TRUE. 
```r
board_register_rsconnect(server = "https://bookdown.org", key = rsc_key, versions = TRUE)
```

Is this change intentional that old behavior has changed ? 

I know the previous way is deprecated and that there is a new way (from https://pins.rstudio.com/reference/board_register.html) but it seems to be the same

``` r
rsc_key <- Sys.getenv("RSC_BOOKDOWN_ORG_TOKEN", unset = "")
board <- board_rsconnect(server = "https://bookdown.org", key = rsc_key)
board$versions
#> [1] FALSE
board_versions_enabled(board, TRUE)
#> [1] FALSE
```
it requires now 
```r
board <- board_rsconnect(server = "https://bookdown.org", key = rsc_key, versions = TRUE)
```
where the `versions` argument is not really documented in `?board_rsconnect`

Hope this quick digging help solves this. 
I think RStudio Connect should support bundle versions by default. And I think this is a breaking change that could cause issue with all existing code because bundles will be remove - I don't think we should do that. 

Also it could have effect with other board.

title: Add slug parameter in pin creation?
description:
I have seen multiple issues that involve changing or renaming a pin, a slug is automatically created for all pins according to their name and some regex rules. This may cause unexpected behavior when saving and retrieving pins. Here some use cases I have can think of or seen personally:

- Users may simply want to rename the pin (but not the original path of the file) for discovery purposes
- Users may want to save a whole new pin inside the same board that happens to create the same slug for different data (say `data&pública.csv`  and `DATA publica.csv`  -> `data-publica.csv`). Yes, not all data users in out there have seen the naming things presentation by Jenny Bryan.

title: Consider splitting the pins package in two packages
description:
The original motivation for the `pins` package was to have an interface for human and machine-readable data catalogs that live in any URL (http://datatxt.org  https://github.com/datatxtorg). Creation of these catalogs and how they are read and created in my opinion should live independently on where the are hosted (S3, github, etc). The R implementation of the `datatxt` specification should have some basic functionality on creation and retrieval of `data.txt`, users should be able to create local boards/folders with the data they want to share for they to then upload to any URL accessible place. 

I see the work around uploading, retrieving, versioning, and synching of data files/pins as something separate that can be handled and extended independently for different providers (azure, github, or any other). 

Having datatxt local boards and their different hosting features in a single package in my opinion obscures the potential of having `datatxt` catalogs accessible in any URL and implemented in multiple programming languages that could eventually improve data interoperability and discovery by simply accessing any domain URL. 

I would be happy to work on this if it makes sense.

Wrong pin content url computed for rsconnect board leading to download error
description:
It could be a edge case because it happens if the url contains a part close to server url 

I stumble upon this on `bookdown.org` while naming the pin `bookdown.org-book-meta`. 

Here is a reprex with a dummy dataset

``` r
pins:::rsconnect_remote_path_from_url(list(server = "bookdown.org"), "https://bookdown.org/cderv/bookdown_org-mtcars/")
#> [1] "-mtcars"
pins:::rsconnect_remote_path_from_url(list(server = "bookdown.org"), "https://bookdown.org/cderv/mtcars/")
#> [1] "/cderv/mtcars"
```

<sup>Created on 2021-03-09 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v1.0.0.9002)</sup>

This happens because the name of the server is used in a `gsub` as a regex string

https://github.com/rstudio/pins/blob/4bef24b6c1783faa0f3151828195ac25ae7dabe0/R/board_rsconnect.R#L328-L334

This means that the `.` in server url will be interpreted as regex dot, leading to `bookdown-org` being matched, and then the remote path being truncated. 

It is easy to workaround but still something not right with the way the remote path is computed from the url.

````r
> packageVersion("pins")
[1] ‘0.4.5.9000’
````

description:
Currently, AWS credential handling is limited to either reading `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` environment variables or having the user explicitly pass these values into `board_register_s3`. The expectation for AWS (based on AWS CLI tools and every AWS SDK) is generally that it should try a whole bunch of ways to access, including:

* [Config files](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-files.html), possibly including profiles, possibly assuming roles
* Using an [external process](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-sourcing-external.html)
* [EC2 Instance Metadata Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-metadata.html), and similar services for ECS/EKS

Consider using paws.storage for S3 access, it will handle all of this.

title: azure_headers function leads to error when LC_TIME locale is not English
description: I've been having trouble trying to pin data to our Azure datalake. When trying to pin to Azure I've been getting a 403 error `The Date header in the request is incorrect.` This was only happening locally, and not when running code in RStudio Connect, and after some digging around (shoutout to @colearendt for teaching me how to properly debug this type of thing) I've come to the realization that the error lies in the way the `date` object gets created in the azure_headers function. `format(Sys.time(), "%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S %Z", tz = "GMT")` Is it possible to input something into the format function to force the locale to be English, rather than the users default language/time format? If not, I feel like it could be a good idea to explicitly state it in an error message that LC_TIME needs to be set to "en_US.UTF-8" or similar. Reprex follows. ``` r ## ICELANDIC # This is my default system setting Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "is_IS.UTF-8") #> [1] "is_IS.UTF-8" # This is what then gets defined as the date within azure_headers() format(Sys.time(), "%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S %Z", tz = "GMT") #> [1] "mán, 15 feb 2021 22:25:58 GMT" library(pins) board_register_azure(container = "data", account = "datalake", key = "my_key_removed", path = "Sandbox") pin(mtcars, "mtcars", board = "azure") #> Error in datatxt_upload_files(board = board, name = name, files = upload_files, : Failed to upload 'data.csv' to 'https://stddatalake.blob.core.windows.net/data/Sandbox/mtcars/data.csv'. Error: #> #> AuthenticationFailed #> Server failed to authenticate the request. Make sure the value of Authorization header is formed correctly including the signature. #> RequestId:fd34161c-401e-0036-50e9-030674000000 #> Time:2021-02-15T22:25:58.8772855Z #> The Date header in the request is incorrect. #> ## US ENGLISH Sys.setlocale("LC_TIME", "en_US.UTF-8") #> [1] "en_US.UTF-8" # This is what then gets defined as the date within azure_headers() format(Sys.time(), "%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S %Z", tz = "GMT") #> [1] "Mon, 15 Feb 2021 22:25:58 GMT" board_register_azure(container = "data", account = "datalake", key = "my_key_removed", path = "Sandbox") #Look ma, no error! :-) pin(mtcars, "mtcars", board = "azure") ``` Created on 2021-02-15 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)

title: rsconnect problems with port 443 and subpaths
description:
There are a handful of related URL parsing problems:

- mismatches on port :443 existing / not existing
- subpaths (i.e. /rsconnect/) not being used, and `server` being used instead of `url` (from the `rsconnect` package)
- token auth issues when port `:443` is defined on the client, but not in the server
- token auth / signature issues (if port mismatch between client and server)
- [port plus a path causing hard-to-debug issues with path creation](https://community.rstudio.com/t/cant-access-pins-using-pin-get-but-i-see-the-pinned-data-in-rstudio-connect/95383/13)

title: Problem in datatxt_refresh_index when subpath is specified
description:
I could be completely wrong with this but I think the `httr::GET` part of `datatxt_refresh_index` fails when the subpath is not null (in my case this is because boards are 'folders' inside an AWS S3 bucket):

```
response <- httr::GET(index_url,
                                   httr::write_disk(temp_index, overwrite = TRUE),
                                   board_datatxt_headers(board, "data.txt"))
```

If I understand the code correctly, this fails because `board_datatxt_headers(board, "data.txt")` is only passed `"data.txt"` but it should have the subpath attached to it. 

In `datatxt_update_index` the `httr::GET` part works, because the index file does have the subpath attached to it:

```
response <- httr::GET(file.path(board$url, index_file_get),
                                   board_datatxt_headers(board, index_file_get))
```
where `index_file_get <- file_path_null(board$subpath, "data.txt")`.

title: curl/httr error in get_pin() / pin_download_one() when file is inside a directory
description:
In brief: when a pin contains a directory with files in it, `get_pin()` fails at the `pin_download_one()` call.

An end-to-end reprex would be hard to share since creating the pin would require the method I am implementing in a package: I am creating a custom pin method following the [Extending pins vignette](https://pins.rstudio.com/articles/pins-extending.html), specifically for Arrow datasets which require the data files to sit in a separate directory.

Below is a limited reprex that uses an [existing pin](https://github.com/petrbouchal/storage-public/tree/main/arrow_ds) created to have files nested in a directory:

``` r
library(pins)
github_public <- pins::board_register_github(repo = "petrbouchal/storage-public", branch = "main")
x <- pin_get("arrow_ds", board = github_public, cache = F)
#> Error in curl::curl_fetch_disk(url, x$path, handle = handle): Failed to open file /var/folders/c8/pj33jytj233g8vr0tw4b2h7m0000gn/T//Rtmp51LbdF/file142807b0d2611/arrow_files/part-0.parquet.
```

<sup>Created on 2021-01-29 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v1.0.0)</sup>

The error occurs  in: https://github.com/rstudio/pins/blob/305bfbc2adfd8089151fa4bd3654c1fed2d3b705/R/pin_download.R#L99-L104

`destination_path` is correctly defined, but if it points to a file in a subdirectory, the `httr::GET()` call fails because that subdirectory has not been created.

I will submit my local fix as a PR for you to consider.

possibly related to #348

title: AWS Authentication Signatures?
description:
Hi @javierluraschi ,

Is pins using [AWS Signature Version 2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/RESTAuthentication.html) headers or the [current, Version 4 header](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/sigv4-auth-using-authorization-header.html)?  From the `s3_board` code, it appears to be construction an authorization header in the V2 format, 

```
Authorization: AWS AWSAccessKeyId:Signature
```

https://github.com/rstudio/pins/blob/f47c2512e0483a7e35e66bac696afc0f49539e5a/R/board_s3.R#L28

Instead of the V4 format, 

```
Authorization: AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 
Credential=AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE/20130524/us-east-1/s3/aws4_request, 
SignedHeaders=host;range;x-amz-date,
Signature=fe5f80f77d5fa3beca038a248ff027d0445342fe2855ddc963176630326f1024
```

Am I following that correctly?  Is there a reason for this or would you please consider moving to the V4 format for authentication?  

I am also unclear why the S3 URL is using `http` and not `https` by default, 

https://github.com/rstudio/pins/blob/f47c2512e0483a7e35e66bac696afc0f49539e5a/R/board_s3.R#L47

Can you fill me in or would you consider moving to HTTPS?  

(Among other concerns, I think these things would also be needed for #255. In fact, using the current signature method and allowing the user to configure the `host` base URL may be all that's necessary to resolve that as well!)

The idea is to send the link to the shiny app to someone, they will open the app and enter a set of inputs, click the button once they are done and create a pin on the company RStudio Connect server. The data that they entered would then be used by another app. Could you please recommend a course of action here? Is it achievable with pins? Are there any security problems associated with this approach?
Here is a stripped down code for the data collection. I get an error trying to put it up on the server in this form (minus the redacted information).
```r
library(shiny)
library(shinyWidgets)
library(pins)
library(dplyr)

board_register_rsconnect(server = "https://connect.example.com", #our server name here
                         key = Sys.getenv("CONNECT_API_KEY")

    numericInputIcon(
      inputId = "number1",
      label = "Some number",

title: Param `name` of `pins::pin_find()` is interpreted as regex
description:
`pins::pin_find()` and `pins::pin_info()` documentation about param **`name`** states:

> The exact name of the pin to match when searching.

Under _Details_ it additionally says:

> For 'local' and 'packages' boards, the 'text' parameter searches the title and description of a pin using a regular expression.

I.e. it says nothing about `name` being interpreted as a regular expression. But it actually is.

```r
pins::pin(x = mtcars,
          board = "local",
          name = "regex.unsafe.[name]")

# nothing found
pins::pin_find(board = "local",
               name = "regex.unsafe.[name]")
#>  A tibble: 0 x 4
#> … with 4 variables: name <chr>, description <chr>, type <chr>, board <chr>

#  wrapping `name` in literal sequence escapes `\\Q...\\E` makes the difference
pins::pin_find(board = "local",
               name = "\\Qregex.unsafe.[name]\\E")
#>  A tibble: 1 x 4
#>  name                description type  board
#>  <chr>               <chr>       <chr> <chr>
#>1 regex.unsafe.[name] ""          table local
```
<sup>Created on 2020-07-19 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org/) (v0.3.0)</sup>

So, my primary question: **Is this the intended behaviour?**

If so, the documentation should be fixed to be more clear, especially because the `name` param of other functions like `pins::pin_get()` and `pins::pin_remove()` is _not_ interpreted as a regular expression.

title: Add support for Put Blocks in Azure
description:
For files larger than 64MB, Pins is unable to use Azure as a Board due to Blob limitations for the current version being used: 
https://github.com/rstudio/pins/blob/master/R/board_azure.R#L3

https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/put-blob

> The maximum size for a block blob created via Put Blob is 256 MB for version 2016-05-31 and later, and 64 MB for older versions. If your blob is larger than 256 MB for version 2016-05-31 and later, or 64 MB for older versions, you must upload it as a set of blocks. For more information, see the Put Block and Put Block Listoperations. It's not necessary to also call Put Blob if you upload the blob as a set of blocks.
> 
> If you attempt to upload a block blob that is larger than 256 MB for version 2016-05-31 and later, and 64 MB for older versions, or a page blob larger than 8 TB, the service returns status code 413 (Request Entity Too Large). The Blob service also returns additional information about the error in the response, including the maximum blob size permitted in bytes.
> 

Using 2019-02-02 could resolve this issue for files smaller than 256 MB, but it would likely be more proper to add functionality to support Put Block for larger files.

pin() fails for remote rsconnect board
description:
When attempting to knit the RMarkdown document in the example pins project included with RStudio Connect (`stock-import.Rmd`) from RStudio Server Pro, `pin(prices, pin_name, board = "rsconnect")` fails with the following error:
```
Error in pin_download(url, name, board$name, headers = rsconnect_api_auth_headers(board,  :    
  Client error: (404) Not Found. Failed to download remote file: https://subdomain.mycompany.com/rsconnecthttps://subdomain.mycompany.com:443/rsconnect/content/7/data.txt
```
where our RStudio Connect server url is `https://subdomain.mycompany.com/rsconnect` (and our RStudio Server Pro url is `https://subdomain.mycompany.com`, if that matters). Traceback:
```
11: report_error(error)
10: pin_download(url, name, board$name, headers = rsconnect_api_auth_headers(board, 
        path, "GET"), custom_etag = etag)
9: rsconnect_api_download(board, entries[[1]]$name, file.path(remote_path, 
       "data.txt"), etag = etag)
8: board_pin_find.rsconnect(board, text = only_name, name = name)
7: board_pin_find(board, text = only_name, name = name)
6: rsconnect_get_by_name(board, name)
5: board_pin_create.rsconnect(board, store_path, name = name, metadata = metadata, 
       ...)
4: board_pin_create(board, store_path, name = name, metadata = metadata, 
       ...)
3: board_pin_store(board, path, name, description, "table", metadata, 
       ...)
2: pin.data.frame(prices, pin_name, board = "rsconnect")
1: pin(prices, pin_name, board = "rsconnect")
```
The problem appears to be due to the below `gsub()` in `rsconnect_remote_path_from_url()` not behaving as intended because there's a port number in `url` but not in `board$server`, and therefore `board$server` doesn't exactly match the prefix of `url`.
```
url <- gsub(paste0("^.*", board$server), "", url)
```
(In this example, `board$server` is `https://subdomain.mycompany.com/rsconnect` and `url` is `https://subdomain.mycompany.com:443/rsconnect/content/7`.)

I've handled this by changing my `CONNECT_SERVER` environment variable from `"https://subdomain.mycompany.com/rsconnect"` to `"https://subdomain.mycompany.com:443/rsconnect"`. However, I wanted to report this here in case 1) this issue impacts anyone else and/or 2) this could be fixed either via documentation or by aligning the way in which urls are reported (with/without port numbers).

title: Allow customization of endpoint for S3 Board (DigitalOcean Spaces)
description:
Thanks for creating `{pins}`! 

I can see that the endpoint for the S3 endpoint is hardcoded to `.s3.amazonaws.com`. 

We use [DigitalOcean Spaces](https://www.digitalocean.com/products/spaces/) as our object storage which is an S3-compatible service, so long as we can change the endpoint to something else (in this case, `<datacenter e.g. sgp1>.digitaloceanspaces.com`. 

If we are able to customize the endpoint (leaving AWS as default), then we would be able to use DigitalOcean Spaces for pins.

Right now, we extend pins by defining a 'dospaces' board using the ff code:

```r
dospaces_headers <- function(board, verb, path, file) {
    date <- format(Sys.time(), "%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S %z")
    # allow full urls to allow arbitrary file downloads
    path <- gsub(paste0(board$url, "/"), "", path, fixed = TRUE)

    content <- paste(
        verb,
        "",
        "application/octet-stream",
        date,
        file.path("", board$bucket, path),
        sep = "\n"
    )

    signature <- openssl::sha1(charToRaw(content), key = board$secret) %>%
        base64enc::base64encode()
    headers <- httr::add_headers(
        Host = paste0(board$bucket, ".", board$datacenter, ".digitaloceanspaces.com"),
        Date = date,
        `Content-Type` = "application/octet-stream",
        Authorization = paste0("AWS ", board$key, ":", signature)
    )

    headers
}

board_initialize.dospaces <- function(
    board,
    bucket = Sys.getenv("PINS_BUCKET"),
    key = Sys.getenv("PINS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"),

    secret = Sys.getenv("PINS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"),
    datacenter = Sys.getenv("PINS_BUCKET_DATACENTER"),
    cache = NULL,
    ...
) {
    board$bucket <- bucket
    board$datacenter <- datacenter
    if (nchar(bucket) == 0) stop("The 'dospaces' board requires a 'bucket' parameter.")
    if (nchar(key) == 0)  stop("The 'dospaces' board requires a 'key' parameter.")
    if (nchar(secret) == 0)  stop("The 'dospaces' board requires a 'secret' parameter.")
    if (nchar(datacenter) == 0) stop("The 'dospaces' board requires a 'datacenter' parameter.")

    dospaces_url <- paste0("https://", board$bucket, ".", board$datacenter, ".digitaloceanspaces.com")

    board_register_datatxt(name = board$name,
                           url = dospaces_url,
                           cache = cache,
                           headers = dospaces_headers,
                           needs_index = FALSE,
                           key = key,
                           secret = secret,
                           bucket = bucket,
                           connect = FALSE,
                           datacenter = datacenter,
                           browse_url = paste0("https://cloud.digitalocean.com/spaces/", bucket))

    board_get(board$name)
}
```

title: Permit multiple attachments to single release in GitHub storage model?
description:
There may be good reasons for `pins` not to do this, so apologies in advance if this doesn't make sense.

I see that `pins` creates a new 'release' for every large file uploaded, while GitHub supports attaching multiple files to a single release (I believe the 2GB limits are only enforced on a per-file basis, not a per-release basis).  

In my existing workflows, I often upload lots of files, and I'm worried about easily bogging down the GitHub API if my repo contains thousands of releases.  

Closely related to this -- most of my uploads are just replacing existing files that I've previously uploaded, and I don't really need to store the full version history.  The GitHub API allows me to overwrite (well, delete and replace) an upload to a released asset.  The current `pins` model with a GitHub backend seems like it is designed to store every single version and never delete something.  I can see the value in that, but it doesn't look like versioning is part of the scope for pins, or that there's any way from within pins to access those old versions, so why not just overwrite files of the same name/description on an existing release instead of creating new releases every time?

title: Add reactive pin_get
description:
When building Shiny applications, it would be helpful to have a `reactive_pin_get()` that automatically invalidates whenever the pin updates (related to #134 for a generic update timestamp and #95 / #140 for additional on-disk caching).

Example:
```r
# from #134 
pin_last_updated <- function(name, board) {
  as.POSIXlt(pin_info(name = name, board = board)$last_deployed_time, format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
}

# from #140
# downside... this only memoises a particular pin_get
memoise_pin_get <- function(name, board, cache = memoise::cache_memory()) {
  memoise::memoise(
    function() pin_get(name = name, board = board, cache = FALSE),
    ~ pin_last_updated(name = name, board = board),
    cache = cache
  )
}

# naive example that takes a memoise cache argument
reactive_pin_get <- function(name, board, intervalMillis, session = getDefaultReactiveDomain(), ...) {
  reactivePoll(
    intervalMillis = intervalMillis, session = session,
    checkFunc = function() pin_last_updated(name = name, board = board),
    valueFunc = memoise_pin_get(name = name, board = board, ...)
  )
}

# checks every 10 seconds
rpin <- reactive_pin_get("iris", "rsconnect", 10000)

# checks every 10 seconds, but also caches to disk
cached_rpin <- reactive_pin_get("iris", "rsconnect", 10000, cache = memoise::cache_filesystem(".pin_cache"))

# to use
rpin()
cached_rpin()
```

description:

I'm not sure whether this line is the root of the issue, or just a symptom of a problem elsewhere, but when trying to find a pin (but the name returns 2 results), we get broken behavior on Connect:

```
# before this line
                            name                                                                   description  type
1  alex.gold/virtual_class_types    Config Vars for Virtual Classrooms. A table pin with 3 rows and 6 columns. table
2 alex.gold/virtual_class_types2 Types (Images) for Virtual Classrooms. A table pin with 2 rows and 9 columns. table

1  alex.gold/virtual_class_types    Config Vars for Virtual Classrooms. A table pin with 3 rows and 6 columns. table {"type":"table","rows":3,"cols":6}
2 alex.gold/virtual_class_types2 Types (Images) for Virtual Classrooms. A table pin with 2 rows and 9 columns. table {"type":"table","rows":2,"cols":9}
```

Because this line messes up the metadata object, later attempts to pull out URLs and such will fail, resulting in an empty set and the pin not returned.

Moreover, debugging this behavior was kinda painful (trying to ensure that the content was where I expected it on Connect, that I had permissions, that `pins` was addressing the right RSC server, etc. All of this information is hidden and not logged). At very least, making some information available in `pin_list` regarding the URL to visit the content directly, or a bit more verbose error logging when things go awry would be very helpful to understand what `pins` is trying to grab.

description: Using the paging API seems to be needed to support kaggle boards with multiple pins, otherwise `pin_find()` won't return all pins; however, `pin_get()` can still properly retrieve any pin.

title: CRAN is requesting no data to be saved in user's home folder
description:
In `pins 0.1.0`, the list of registered boards and default local board is stored in `~/.pins`; however, CRAN is requesting this to not be the default since packages are not allowed to write outside the temp folder without user consent.

Instead, we need to opt-in to all boards and let users choose where data is stored by explicitly calling:

```
board_register_local()
```

The default board should become a `temp` board that makes use of the temp folder only, anything else would have to be explicitly requested by the user.

title: Support for caching in pin_get()
description:
Caching is currently only supported in `pin()`, should be enabled in `pin_get()` as well, example:

```
pins::pin_get("gunnvant/game-of-thrones-srt", "kaggle") %>%
    dir(full.names = TRUE) %>%
    purrr::map(~jsonlite::read_json(.x)) %>%
    unlist() %>%
    tibble::tibble(captions = .)
```

In addition, when a zip is downloaded it should return all files, not the folder, such that the following works:

```
pins::pin_get("gunnvant/game-of-thrones-srt", "kaggle") %>%
    purrr::map(~jsonlite::read_json(.x)) %>%
    unlist() %>%
    tibble::tibble(captions = .)
```
